Brands made AI the pitch. The audience made it the penalty

The numbers turned. Announcing AI now costs trust. Making something real is the move.

01 Field notes

Record spend, thin interaction

A June 2026 Harris Poll found 78 percent of consumers say AI makes ads feel less authentic, 73 percent are less likely to trust an ad they suspect was AI made, and 63 percent are less likely to buy from a brand that runs one. Excitement about AI fell from 50 percent to 19 percent in two years. Leading with AI now reads as a brand that did not care enough to make something real.

The activations that convert answer back

AI as infrastructure wins. AI as the headline loses. And the antidote to a feed full of synthetic content is the opposite of a feed: something physical, in the room, that a person cannot fake and a model cannot flood.

03 Craft

Meanwhile, done right

The brands pulling ahead use AI quietly to move faster and test more, then spend the saved time on real, human moments. Only 26 percent of consumers now prefer generative AI creator content, down from 60 percent in 2023. The winners hide the machine and show the craft.
